Wrote the screener output and re-checked each cited line (output.py 50-70/114-117, keywords.py 33/66, formatter.py 26-30/193-202, tests/test_format.py 159-175 & 653-701, pyproject.toml 1-3/38-39, CHANGELOG 12-26).

- Output: `/home/mara/cwe-bench/pipelines/stacking/out/screener/326.json`
- Trust decision: each output formatter must escape whatever in a SQL token can terminate or reinterpret the literal it emits, decided per token in the filter's escape branch — quote-only escaping is insufficient, backslashes must be doubled first (`sqlparse/filters/output.py:65-67`, `output.py:114-116`).
- `pattern_fit`: B (fix is two mirrored classes in one file; the same sink still lacks line-terminator escaping and PHP `$` escaping).
- Strongest lever: "reason to dismiss" — the project's own test keeps CR/CRLF inside literals untouched (`tests/test_format.py:159-175`), so a solver can justify leaving the raw-newline/CR route into the generated Python literal open.
- Biggest red flag: `tiny_repo` (~3.5k lines, ~0.2 MB) — landing point is one obvious file, so the 45-minute fairness bar is easy but the hardness rests almost entirely on the uncovered-route argument.
